summary: A clean baseball list with a good spread: the Yankees, Red Sox and Dodgers are gimmes, and the old A's, Reds and Pirates dynasties are fair stretches. Famous teams with few titles (Cubs, Mets, Astros) burn lives fast, but each one shows its count.
reasons: Casual found 6 (Yankees, Red Sox, Dodgers, Giants, Cardinals, Braves), then ran out of lives on the Cubs, Mets, Astros, White Sox and Phillies, each showing its title count.

Data is current (2025 Dodgers and 2026 Brewers titles counted) and franchise counts include old cities. Nicknames, cities and old names all work, and the subject words and other sports' teams are free.
Tough for players who don't follow baseball: 20 of the 30 teams cost a life, so it sits at the low edge of the daily target.
fixes: 'boston' should mean the Red Sox. Right now it offers 'Atlanta Braves / Boston Red Sox' with the Braves first, and once the Red Sox are found it turns into 'did you mean Atlanta Braves', because the Braves have the bare alias 'Boston'. Drop 'Boston' from the Braves and keep 'Boston Braves'. This is the same class as New York, Philadelphia, Kansas City and Milwaukee, which are already in junkAliases. junkAliases applies to the whole topic, so check that 'boston' still reaches the Red Sox afterwards.

Add to junkAliases the redirects that aren't names of a team: 'Carlos Ahern' (Red Sox), 'SFG Productions' (Giants), and the mascots 'Tessie the Green Monster' (Red Sox) and 'Captain jolly roger' (Pirates).

Old nicknames on their own aren't recognized: 'indians' (Cleveland Guardians, 2) and 'expos' (Washington Nationals, 1) say they aren't answers for this list when they should show the count. Add 'Indians' and 'Expos' as aliases.
